questions.q: How does Account Monitor differ from the Inquire on Detail Balances page?
options: It is identical, just a renamed version of the same page
It only shows budget data, never actuals
It continuously watches a predefined set of accounts and flags them automatically, rather than requiring a deliberate one-off lookup
It can only be used at year-end
questions.explain: Account Monitor is a self-updating watchlist with tolerances, unlike the deliberate, one-time lookup of Inquire on Detail Balances.

questions.q: What is a tolerance rule in Account Monitor?
options: A rule that deletes accounts automatically
A threshold, in amount or percentage, that triggers a visual flag when crossed
The number of decimal places shown on a balance
A rule restricting who can post journals
questions.explain: A tolerance defines the amount or percentage threshold that, once crossed, causes the account to flag automatically.

questions.q: Where does Account Monitor commonly appear for a user?
options: Only inside the Journal Approvals workflow
Only in the Chart of Accounts setup pages
The General Accounting Dashboard and the Financial Reporting Center
Only inside the Subledger Accounting rules engine
questions.explain: Account Monitor is surfaced on the General Accounting Dashboard and alongside other tools in the Financial Reporting Center.

questions.q: LTV Manufacturing Corporation sets a tolerance to flag Travel & Entertainment if PTD actual exceeds 110% of PTD budget. If PTD actual is $16,940 against a $15,000 PTD budget, what happens?
options: Nothing, because the account is under budget
The account is flagged, since actual is about 112.9% of budget, above the 110% threshold
The period is automatically closed
The tolerance resets to zero
questions.explain: 16,940 / 15,000 is roughly 112.9%, which exceeds the 110% tolerance, so the account flags automatically.

questions.q: Why is Account Monitor described as changing accountants from reactive to proactive?
options: Because it eliminates the need for any General Ledger reports ever again
Because tolerances are defined once and flags appear on their own as journals post, instead of waiting for someone to notice a number looks off in a report
Because it automatically posts journals without approval
Because it replaces the need for a chart of accounts
questions.explain: Instead of catching issues only when someone happens to run and review a report, Account Monitor surfaces deviations automatically as they occur.
